text: The central referee holds supreme authority over match conduct, safety interventions, and score announcements. Under Art. 1.3, the referee intervenes immediately when an athlete commits a serious or severe foul, entangles fingers inside a sleeve or pant cuff, exits the safety area, or faces imminent joint or cervical injury in youth and white belt divisions.
title: IBJJF Art. 1.1-1.3: Referee Authority, Match Intervention, and Gestures

text: Matches conclude by Submission (Art. 2.2.1: physical tap, verbal tap, or scream), Stoppage/Loss of Consciousness, Disqualification, or Regulation Scoreboard Hierarchy. When regulation time expires without submission or DQ, victory goes strictly in order to: (1) Most Points, (2) Most Advantages if points are tied, (3) Fewest Penalties if points and advantages are both tied, and (4) Referee Decision (Art. 2.2.5) if points, advantages, and penalties are completely equal (for example 0-0 pts, 1-1 penalty adv, 2-2 pen). In a Referee Decision, referees evaluate which athlete displayed greater offensive initiative, closer near-scoring sweeps or passes, and credible submission attempts across regulation.
title: IBJJF Art. 2.2: Victory Conditions and Regulation Tie-Breaker Hierarchy

text: All IBJJF point-scoring positions (Takedown, Sweep, Knee on Belly, Guard Pass, Mount, and Back Control) require 3 full seconds of clear positional stabilization inside the match area before points are awarded. Points are cumulative when an athlete chains distinct scoring actions (for example +2 Sweep directly into +4 Mount = +6 total points after 3s mount stabilization). Crucial submission-defense exception: if the bottom athlete locks a credible submission hold during a pass or sweep, points are withheld until the top athlete completely frees themselves from the submission and stabilizes for 3 seconds. Regulation durations: Adult White 5m, Blue 6m, Purple 7m, Brown 8m, Black 10m; Master divisions and Juvenile divisions run 5 minutes.
title: IBJJF Art. 3.1 & Art. 4: 3-Second Stabilization Rule and Match Durations

text: Awarded 2 points when an athlete initiates a projection or takedown from standing (both athletes on their feet, or countering a guard pull before the guard puller sits cleanly) and holds the opponent on their back, side, or Seated/Turtle with top control for 3 seconds in-bounds. If the opponent lands on all fours (Turtle), the attacking athlete must control behind the shoulder/hip line for 3 seconds to score 2 points. Takedowns initiated in-bounds that land out-of-bounds with clear control still score or earn an advantage per Art. 4.1.4; stabilizing for less than 3 seconds (0.8s to 2.9s) downgrades to +1 Advantage under Art. 5.2.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.1: Takedown (2 Points)

text: Awarded 3 points when the athlete in top position clears the bottom athlete's legs (closed, open, half, butterfly, or spider guard) and establishes perpendicular Side Control, North-South, Mount, or Knee on Belly for 3 full seconds with the opponent's back or side pinned and free of any submission lock. If the bottom athlete turns to Turtle before 3 seconds of back-pinned control elapse, no 3-point pass is scored; instead, the top passer receives +1 Advantage under Art. 5.2 for forcing the defensive turtle turn.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.2: Guard Pass (3 Points)

text: Awarded 2 points when the top athlete places the knee or shin nearest the opponent's hips across the opponent's abdomen/chest while posting the outside foot flat on the mat (toes engaged, knee off the mat) facing the opponent and maintaining posture for 3 seconds. Keeping the outside knee on the mat or holding for less than 3 seconds yields +1 Advantage under Art. 5.2 rather than 2 points.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.3: Knee on Belly (2 Points)

text: Awarded 4 points when the top athlete straddles the opponent's torso (opponent on back, side, or flat stomach) with both knees or one knee and one foot touching the mat for 3 seconds, without being trapped in half guard and with at least one opponent arm maximum inside the legs. Trapping BOTH of the opponent's arms inside the legs (double-arm high mount) scores 0 points; standard Mount, Technical Mount, and S-Mount over a single shoulder score 4 points.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.4: Mount and S-Mount / Back Mount (4 Points)

text: Awarded 4 points when the athlete controls the opponent's back and places both heels inside the opponent's inner thighs (hooks) or locks a Figure-Four Body Triangle around the waist for 3 full seconds, without crossing the ankles over each other between the thighs and without trapping both of the opponent's arms inside the legs. Securing only one hook or losing the second hook before 3 seconds elapse awards +1 Advantage.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.5: Back Control with Hooks or Body Triangle (4 Points)

text: Awarded 2 points when the bottom athlete, starting with any form of guard (closed, half, butterfly, open, or single-leg wrestle-up initiated from guard), inverts top and bottom positions and stabilizes on top for 3 seconds in-bounds. When a wrestle-up from guard forces the top player onto hands and knees in Turtle, the sweeping athlete must clear any remaining leg entanglement and control behind the opponent's hips/shoulders for 3 seconds (or flatten them) to earn 2 sweep points. Reversals from bottom Side Control, Mount, or bottom Turtle without first establishing guard score 0 sweep points.
title: IBJJF Art. 4.6: Sweep from Guard (2 Points)

text: An Advantage (+1 adv) is awarded when an athlete: (1) achieves a point-scoring position (Takedown, Sweep, Pass, Knee on Belly, Mount, or Back) but holds it for less than 3 seconds before the opponent escapes or time expires; (2) forces the opponent out of bounds mid-sweep or mid-pass; (3) forces the opponent into defensive Turtle or half-guard squeeze to prevent a pass; or (4) applies a real submission threat that places the opponent in genuine danger and forces active defensive escape (assessed after the hold ends). Merely grabbing the head for an arm-out gi guillotine without real choking threat scores 0 technical advantages.
title: IBJJF Art. 5.1 & 5.2: Advantage Scoring Criteria and Sub-3s Downgrades

text: Minor / Serious Technical Fouls follow the strict IBJJF 4-step Penalty Cascade (Art. 5.3 & 7.2): 1st Penalty = recorded penalty on offender (0 bonus to opponent); 2nd Penalty = recorded penalty + opponent receives +1 Advantage; 3rd Penalty = recorded penalty + opponent receives +2 Points; 4th Penalty = Immediate Disqualification (DQ) of offender. Lack of Combativeness / Stalling (Art. 6.3.2 A/B): when one or both athletes stall without seeking positional progression or submission for 20 continuous seconds, the referee issues stalling penalties. In Double Stalling (for example top player stalling head-down in closed guard while bottom player holds closed guard without attacking for 20s), BOTH athletes receive simultaneous penalties: 1st double stalling -> 1-1 pen (0-0 adv); 2nd double stalling -> 2-2 pen and BOTH athletes automatically receive +1 penalty advantage (1-1 adv).
title: IBJJF Art. 5.3, 6.3.2 & 7.2: Penalty Cascade, 20s Stalling, and Double Stalling

text: Common IBJJF Technical / Minor Fouls penalized via the Art. 7.2 cascade rather than instant DQ: (1) Art. 6.3.2 (F) Fingers Inside Sleeve or Pant Cuff: hooking one or more fingers inside the opening of the opponent's kimono sleeve cuff or pant leg hem causes immediate referee grip-strip, neutral grip reset, and 1 minor foul penalty (use a four-finger outside pistol or pocket grip). (2) Art. 6.3.2 (J) Guard Pull Without Contact Grip: sitting down or pulling guard without an established physical grip on the opponent draws a referee stand-up and 1 penalty. (3) Art. 6.3.2 (C) Fleeing Mat Bounds: deliberately Crawling/running out of the match area to avoid a takedown, sweep, or pass draws 1 penalty (+2 pts to opponent if avoiding clean score), whereas fleeing an active locked submission out of bounds is an immediate DQ under Art. 6.2.3 (D). (4) Art. 6.3.2 (G) No-Gi Cloth Gripping: grabbing rashguard, shorts, or belt in No-Gi draws 1 penalty.
title: IBJJF Art. 6.3.2 (C/F/G/J): Cuff Grips, Guard Pull Without Grip, Out-of-Bounds, and No-Gi Cloth

text: The following techniques trigger immediate Disqualification (DQ) across ALL age divisions (Juvenile, Adult, Master), ALL belt ranks (White through Black), and BOTH Gi and No-Gi: (A) Slamming an opponent onto the mat from guard or to escape a submission (`slam`); (B/F) Spinal locks, neck cranks, crucifix cranks, or Twister without an accompanying choke (`spinal_lock_without_choke`); (J) Scissor takedown / Kani Basami (`scissor_takedown`); (V) Suplex landing the opponent on their head or neck (`suplex_head_neck`); (N) Small-joint manipulation bending fewer than four fingers or toes (`small_joint_manipulation`).
title: IBJJF Art. 6.2.3 (A/B/F/J/N/V): Universal Severe Technical Fouls (Immediate DQ All Belts)

text: Division-specific IBJJF prohibitions under Art. 6.2.2 Table of Illegal Moves: (1) Jumping Closed Guard (#5, `jumping_closed_guard`): ILLEGAL (Immediate DQ) at White Belt (Juvenile, Adult, and Master, Gi & No-Gi) whenever both feet leave the mat to jump into closed guard against a standing opponent, including flying triangles and flying armbars. Legal from Blue Belt upward. White belts MUST keep one foot planted or frame a foot on the hip while sitting. (2) Wristlocks (#12, `wristlock`): ILLEGAL (Immediate DQ) for ALL White Belts and ALL Juvenile divisions (including Juvenile Blue/Purple); LEGAL for Adult and Master Blue, Purple, Brown, and Black belts. (3) Single-Leg Takedown with Head Outside (#21, `single_leg_head_outside`): ILLEGAL (Immediate DQ) for White Belts and Juveniles when driving the opponent's head/neck downward with the attacker's head to the outside of the hip; LEGAL for Adult and Master Blue Belt and above.
title: IBJJF Art. 6.2.2 (#5, #12, #21): White Belt Jumping Guard, Wristlocks, and Head-Outside Single Leg

text: Under IBJJF Art. 6.2.2 (#14-#17), Bicep Slicer (`bicep_slicer`), Calf Slicer (`calf_slicer`), Straight Kneebar (`kneebar`), and Toe Hold (`toe_hold`) are LEGAL in Adult and Master Brown Belt and Black Belt divisions (both Gi and No-Gi), and ILLEGAL (Immediate DQ) at White, Blue, and Purple Belt as well as all Juvenile divisions. Straight Ankle / Foot Lock (#13) is legal from White Belt upward ONLY when turning outward toward the unattacked side without reaping across the centerline.
title: IBJJF Art. 6.2.2 (#14-17): Kneebar, Toe Hold, Bicep Slicer, Calf Slicer, and Straight Footlock

text: Inside and Outside Heel Hooks (`heel_hook`, Art. 6.2.3 K) and Knee Reaping (`knee_reap`, Art. 6.2.3 M: crossing the outside thigh from outside-in across the opponent's trapped/standing leg past the hip-knee line forcing inward knee rotation) are LEGAL EXCLUSIVELY in Adult Brown Belt No-Gi and Adult Black Belt No-Gi divisions. They remain an IMMEDIATE DISQUALIFICATION (DQ) in ALL Gi divisions (including Adult Black Belt Gi), ALL Master divisions (including Master 1-7 Brown/Black No-Gi), ALL Juvenile divisions, and ALL White, Blue, and Purple Belt divisions.
title: IBJJF Art. 6.2.3 (K/M): Heel Hooks and Knee Reaping - Adult Brown/Black No-Gi Exception

text: Under IBJJF Art. 8, Gi competitors must wear clean white, royal blue, or black woven cotton kimonos passing the Official IBJJF Gi Checker Tool (4-finger internal sleeve clearance, sleeve reaching within 5 cm of wrist, pants within 5 cm of ankle bone, belt tied with double knot and 20-30 cm tails). No-Gi athletes must wear a ranked rashguard showing at least 10% belt color and board shorts free of pockets, zippers, or metal. Under Art. 6.1, unsportsmanlike conduct, disrespecting officials, or coaching inside the barricaded area results in disciplinary DQ.
title: IBJJF Art. 6.1 & Art. 8: Gi Inspection, No-Gi Attire, and Disciplinary Conduct

When the athlete taps the ground twice with his/her foot, when arms are trapped by opponent. When the athlete verbally withdraws, requesting the match be stopped. When the athlete screams or emits noise expressing pain while trapped in a submission hold. Stoppage When one of the athletes alleges to be suffering from cramps, the opponent shall be declared winner of the match. When the referee perceives that a hold in place may expose the athlete to serious physical injury. Advantages: When there is a draw in the number of points, the athlete with the most advantage points shall be declared the winner. Penalties: When there is a draw in the number of points and advantage points, the athlete with the least penalty points counted against him/her shall be declared the winner. text: [Page 24] 24 ARTICLE 5 - ADVANTAGES An advantage-point is counted when an athlete achieves a point-scoring pass position requiring 3 (three) seconds of control but is unable to maintain control for the entire duration. An advantage is characterized by near-completion of a point-scoring position. The referee should assess whether the opponent was in any real danger and if the athlete clearly came close to reaching the point- scoring pass position. The athlete shall be awarded an advantage-point when he/she attempts a submission hold where the opponent is in real danger of submitting. Again, it is the referee's duty to assess how close the submission hold came to fruition. 5 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.4 5.5 5.6 5.6.1 5.6.2 An advantage point may be awarded by the referee even after a match has run its course but before announcing the result. text: [Page 34] 34 ARTICLE 7 - PENALTIES Penalties are awarded by referees with the aim of assuring the match flows properly and that the rules of the sport and the competition are being respected. » Severe Fouls » Serious Fouls » Penalties for Lack of Combativeness Severe Penalties » Technical Penalties: Summary disqualification from the match at the moment of the infraction. » Disciplinary Penalties: Summary disqualification from the match and competition at the moment of the infraction. If an athlete is disqualified from a gi event and is also signed up for no-gi, he or she will be disqualified from both events. Serious Penalties Referees shall abide by the following series of penalties. • 1st PENALTY - The referee will mark the first penalty for the athlete. • 2nd PENALTY - Advantage point concession to opponent of penalized athlete and second penalty marked on scoreboard for perpetrating athlete. •
